title: Nightly E2E Health — suites table
description: The structured `suites` input of the nightly-e2e-health reusable workflow. Passed as a JSON string because workflow_call inputs cannot be objects. Validated by check-nightly-e2e-health.mjs BEFORE any API call, so a malformed table fails the gate rather than silently gating less than its author believes. Deliberately NOT a delimiter-joined mini-language: a `;`-separated table cannot express optional per-suite freshness, cannot distinguish an exact job name from a pattern, and cannot reject a duplicate.

label.description: Human-readable name for this suite, used in the report. Must be unique across the table — two suites sharing a label produce one report line for two verdicts.

workflow.description: Workflow FILE name (e.g. `maestro-e2e.yml`). The Actions API accepts the file name as the workflow id, which survives a rename of the workflow's display `name:`. A file the API cannot find is a hard failure, not a missing-evidence bootstrap: it means the workflow was renamed or deleted out from under the gate.

match.description: How this suite's verdict is read. `run` and `job` are the machine-readable contract and are preferred; `job_pattern` is a last resort for matrix job names no single string can cover.

freshness_hours.description: Override the workflow-level freshness window for this suite. A run older than this is treated as no run at all (missing evidence), which fails once the bootstrap window has closed.

required_sha.description: When present, the run's head_sha must equal this exact commit. Use only where the suite is expected to run on a pinned commit; freshness plus the branch filter is the normal staleness control.

first_seen.description: ISO-8601 UTC timestamp naming when this suite entered the table — the ANCHOR of its per-suite grace window (truth-table rows 27-30). Set it when you ADD a suite to an already-armed repo: for `grace_days` (default 14) from this instant, MISSING evidence for THIS suite reports with its expiry but does not block, while every other suite stays armed. Evidence of FAILURE blocks inside the window too. It may NOT be in the future — a future anchor would be a hand-typed expiry under another name, extendable forever by one string edit — and a window running beyond `bootstrap_max_days` FAILS as misconfiguration rather than being clamped. A lapsed anchor is inert, so the field can be left in place.

grace_days.description: How many days after `first_seen` this suite's grace window lasts. Default 14. Requires `first_seen` — a grace length with no anchor forgives nothing and reads as though it forgives everything. Bounded by the same ceiling as the bootstrap window (`bootstrap_max_days`, hard ceiling 30): per-suite grace spends from the same forgiveness budget, and a grace that could outlive that ceiling is acmeorga's forever-bootstrap wearing a per-suite hat.

matchRun.description: Read the run's own conclusion. Correct when the whole workflow IS the suite.

name.description: The job's name, EXACTLY as the Actions API reports it. For a job inside a nested reusable workflow the API reports `<caller job name> / <called job name>` — the same composition the required status-check context uses. A run that completes without ever producing this job is a renamed job, which fails once bootstrap closes.

matchJob.description: Read one named job's conclusion. Correct when the suite is one job inside a larger workflow (so a Lighthouse regression elsewhere in that workflow cannot block every PR).

pattern.description: An ECMAScript regular expression ANCHORED at both ends. Anchoring is enforced, not advised: an unanchored regex is a substring test wearing a regex's clothes, so `Playwright` would match `Playwright (skipped placeholder)`. Matching ZERO jobs is an error — zero matches is the signature of a renamed job, which is exactly how a gate stops gating unnoticed. Any non-success match decides the verdict.

matchJobPattern.description: Read every job whose name matches an anchored regex. Last resort: use it only for matrix job names (`… (android)`, `… (shard 2/4)`) that no single exact string can cover.
